newsitem.title: MEXICO: Rising confidence bolsters peso - Mexico cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Rising confidence bolsters peso - Mexico cenbank.

text.p: Current strength in the Mexican peso is a product of greater confidence in the Mexican economy both domestically and abroad, Mexico's central bank governor said on Wednesday.
Banco de Mexico governor Miguel Mancera told reporters that declining inflation was helping to bolster the currency.
"I believe this phenomenon is a product fundamentally of the improved confidence in the economy, and the performance of inflation," he said.
"People are looking (at the peso) from the perspective of declining inflation, and given the level of interest rates, then it doesn't look attractive to buy dollars," he added.
"What's more, we see foreigners say it is attractive to invest in pesos from a perspective of stability...," he said.
The peso has held stable for most of this year, beginning 1997 at 7.890 to the dollar and closing on Wednesday at 7.896.
